literal: Events were sudden; troops and horses were not yet arrayed. Seeing this, the Later Lord also wished to withdraw eastward.
idiomatic: Events had come in a rush; troops and horses were not yet in order. Seeing the field, Emperor Wucheng wished to withdraw eastward.

literal: Soon he accepted Prince of Hejian Xiaowan's request and ordered Prince of Zhao Commandery to take overall command of the generals.
idiomatic: Soon he accepted Prince of Hejian Xiaowan's plea and put Prince of Zhao Commandery in overall charge of the generals.

literal: After heavy snow, the Zhou men made infantry their vanguard, descending from the western hills — two li from the city.
idiomatic: After heavy snow, the Zhou made infantry their vanguard, descending from the western hills two li from the city.

literal: All the generals wished to meet them with a counterattack.
idiomatic: Every general wanted to meet them with a counterattack.

literal: An edict said, "Infantry by nature have limited momentum. With the snow so deep, a meeting engagement is ill advised — better to hold formation and wait.
idiomatic: An edict ran, "Infantry can only push so far. With snow this deep, a meeting fight is ill advised — hold your lines and wait.

literal: They will be weary and we rested — defeat is certain.
idiomatic: They will be weary and we rested — the victory is certain.

literal: " Battle was joined and the enemy was routed. The vanguard was annihilated to the last man; the rest fled through the night.
idiomatic: " Battle was joined and the enemy was routed. The vanguard was annihilated to the last man; the rest fled through the night.

literal: Shao was then ordered to lead cavalry in pursuit; he could not overtake them before the frontier and returned.
idiomatic: Shao was ordered to lead cavalry in pursuit — he could not overtake them before the frontier and turned back.

literal: The Later Lord commended his merit, separately enfeoffed him Duke of Wude Commandery in Huai Province, and advanced him to Grand Preceptor.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng commended his merit, separately enfeoffed him duke of Wude Commandery in Huai Province, and advanced him to grand preceptor.

literal: The mother of Zhou chancellor Yuwen Hu, Lady Yan, had first been assigned to Zhongshan Palace. Learning that Yan still lived, Hu sent a letter through the border asking for his mother's return and proposing neighborly peace.
idiomatic: The mother of Zhou chancellor Yuwen Hu, Lady Yan, had first been assigned to Zhongshan Palace. Learning she still lived, Hu sent a letter through the border asking for her return and proposing neighborly peace.

literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; Shao encamped below the passes.
idiomatic: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; Shao encamped below the passes.

literal: The Later Lord sent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Xu Shirong by fast relay with the Zhou letter to consult Shao.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng sent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Xu Shirong by fast relay with the Zhou letter to consult Shao.

literal: Shao said the Zhou were fickle and had never kept faith; the affair at Jinyang had already shown as much.
idiomatic: Shao said the Zhou were fickle and had never kept faith — the affair at Jinyang had already shown as much.

literal: Hu outwardly styled himself chancellor but was in truth a king. Having asked peace for his mother's sake, he sent not a single envoy to state his case — yet we would return her on the strength of a letter alone. That would look like weakness.
idiomatic: Hu outwardly styled himself chancellor but was in truth a king. He asked peace for his mother's sake, yet sent not a single envoy to state his case — and we would return her on the strength of a letter alone. That would look like weakness.

literal: In my humble view, we should agree outwardly and release her later — that would not be too late.
idiomatic: In my humble view, we should agree outwardly and release her later — that would not be too late.

literal: He was not heeded.
idiomatic: He was not heeded.

literal: An envoy was then sent to escort her back with full ceremony.
idiomatic: An envoy was sent to escort her back with full ceremony.

literal: Once Hu had his mother, he still sent generals Yuchi Jiong and others to strike at Luoyang.
idiomatic: Once Hu had his mother, he still sent generals Yuchi Jiong and others to strike at Luoyang.

literal: An edict dispatched Prince of Lanling Chang Gong and Grand General Hulü Guang with troops to attack them; they encamped below Mount Mang and lingered without advancing.
idiomatic: An edict dispatched Prince of Lanling Gao Chang Gong and Grand General Hulü Guang with troops to attack them. They encamped below Mount Mang and lingered without advancing.

literal: The Later Lord summoned Shao and said, "I wish to send you to the siege at Luoyang — but the Turks are here and must still be held in check. What do you think?
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng summoned Shao and said, "I wish to send you to the siege at Luoyang — but the Turks are here and must still be held in check. What do you think?

literal: " Shao said, "Northern barbarians on the frontier are a matter of scabies; the Western Qiang pressing in are a disease in the vitals. I beg leave to go south as ordered.
idiomatic: " Shao said, "Northern raiders on the frontier are scabies; the Western Qiang pressing in are a disease in the vitals. I beg leave to go south as ordered.

literal: " The Later Lord said, "My mind is the same.
idiomatic: " Emperor Wucheng said, "My mind is the same.

literal: " He then ordered Shao to command a thousand elite cavalry, setting out from Jinyang.
idiomatic: " He ordered Shao to command a thousand elite cavalry and set out from Jinyang.

literal: In five days he had crossed the river and joined the grand generals in deliberating advance and halt.
idiomatic: In five days he had crossed the river and joined the grand generals in weighing advance and halt.

literal: At dawn Shao led two hundred cavalry from his personal retinue and climbed the Mang slopes with the other armies to take a brief look at the Zhou disposition.
idiomatic: At dawn Shao led two hundred cavalry from his personal retinue and climbed the Mang slopes with the other armies to take a brief look at the Zhou disposition.

literal: At Dahe Valley they ran straight into the Zhou army; he at once sent riders racing to the camps to muster troops and horses.
idiomatic: At Dahe Valley they ran straight into the Zhou army; he at once sent riders racing to the camps to muster troops and horses.

literal: He then formed battle lines with the generals and waited.
idiomatic: He then formed battle lines with the generals and waited.

literal: Shao took the left wing, Prince of Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right — facing the Zhou.
idiomatic: Shao took the left wing, Prince of Lanling the center, and Hulü Guang the right — facing the Zhou.

literal: Shao shouted across to the Zhou, "You, Yuwen Hu — you have just recovered your mother and cannot repay kindness with gratitude. What do you mean by coming today?
idiomatic: Shao shouted across to the Zhou, "You, Yuwen Hu — you have just recovered your mother and cannot repay kindness with gratitude. What do you mean by coming today?

literal: " The Zhou answered, "Heaven sent us — what is there to ask?
idiomatic: " The Zhou answered, "Heaven sent us — what is there to ask?

literal: " Shao said, "Heaven rewards the good and punishes the evil — it has sent you here to die.
idiomatic: " Shao said, "Heaven rewards the good and punishes the evil — it has sent you here to die.

literal: " The Zhou army again put infantry in front and came up the hill to fight.
idiomatic: " The Zhou army again put infantry in front and came up the hill to fight.

literal: Shao, seeing their foot soldiers against his cavalry, withdrew step by step and drew them on until their strength failed — then ordered his men to dismount and strike.
idiomatic: Shao, seeing foot soldiers against his cavalry, withdrew step by step and drew them on until their strength failed — then ordered his men to dismount and strike.

literal: Close combat had barely begun when the Zhou broke completely.
idiomatic: Close combat had barely begun when the Zhou broke completely.

literal: Those who met the center wing collapsed at once as well; very many fell into ravines and gullies and died.
idiomatic: Those who met the center wing collapsed at once as well; very many fell into ravines and gullies and died.

literal: The siege of Luoyang also broke and fled, abandoning all camps and tents; from Mount Mang to Gushui for thirty li, military stores and equipment filled the streams and marshes.
idiomatic: The siege of Luoyang also broke and fled, abandoning all camps and tents. From Mount Mang to Gushui for thirty li, military stores and equipment filled the streams and marshes.

literal: The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers; at Heyin a great feast of wine was set out, merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed Duke of Lingwu County.
idiomatic: The imperial carriage visited Luoyang and personally encouraged the soldiers. At Heyin a great feast of wine was set out; merits were assessed and rewards given — Shao was made grand preceptor and enfeoffed duke of Lingwu County.

literal: In the third year of Tiantong he was made Left Chancellor, Duke of Yongchang Commandery, with revenue from Cang Province.
idiomatic: In the third year of Tiantong he was made left chancellor, duke of Yongchang Commandery, with revenue from Cang Province.

literal: In the first month of the second year of Wuping he marched out by the Jinzhou route, reached Dinglong, built the two fortresses Weidi and Pingkou, and returned.
idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Wuping he marched out by the Jinzhou route, reached Dinglong, built the two fortresses Weidi and Pingkou, and returned.

literal: In the second month Zhou troops came raiding; Shao was sent with Right Chancellor Hulü Guang and Grand Commandant Prince of Lanling Chang Gong to repel them.
idiomatic: In the second month Zhou troops came raiding; Shao was sent with Right Chancellor Hulü Guang and Grand Commandant Prince of Lanling Gao Chang Gong to repel them.

literal: At the end of the third month they marched and reached the western frontier.
idiomatic: At the end of the third month they marched and reached the western frontier.

literal: There was a fortress called Baigu — an enemy stronghold of absolute peril, a stone citadel a thousand ren high; none of the generals would agree to besiege it.
idiomatic: There was a fortress called Baigu — an enemy stronghold of absolute peril, a stone citadel a thousand ren high — and none of the generals would agree to besiege it.

literal: Shao said, "North of the Fen and east of the Yellow River are lands the state must hold. If Baigu is not taken, the matter is like a chronic disease.
idiomatic: Shao said, "North of the Fen and east of the Yellow River are lands the state must hold. If Baigu is not taken, the matter is like a chronic disease.

literal: I reckon their relief will come by the southern road; if we cut that vital route, rescue cannot arrive.
idiomatic: I reckon their relief will come by the southern road; if we cut that vital route, rescue cannot arrive.

literal: And though the fortress stands high, within it is very narrow — fire-arrows shot into it could destroy it in a day.
idiomatic: And though the fortress stands high, within it is very narrow — fire-arrows shot into it could destroy it in a day.

literal: " The generals approved; drums were sounded and the attack began.
idiomatic: " The generals approved; drums were sounded and the attack began.

literal: The fortress fell; Yitong Xue Jingli was captured; heads and captives were taken in great numbers; they then walled Huagu, garrisoned it, and returned.
idiomatic: The fortress fell; Yitong Xue Jingli was captured; heads and captives were taken in great numbers. They then walled Huagu, garrisoned it, and returned.

literal: He was enfeoffed Duke of Guangping Commandery.
idiomatic: He was enfeoffed duke of Guangping Commandery.

literal: That month Zhou again sent generals to raid the frontier.
idiomatic: That month Zhou again sent generals to raid the frontier.

literal: Right Chancellor Hulü Guang led troops out first to attack; Shao also asked to go.
idiomatic: Right Chancellor Hulü Guang led troops out first to attack; Shao also asked to go.

literal: In the fifth month they captured and subdued Qincheng.
idiomatic: In the fifth month they captured and subdued Qincheng.

literal: The Zhou at the south of Yaoxiang raised a new walled town, linking east to Dingyang, and dug a deep trench to cut the road.
idiomatic: The Zhou south of Yaoxiang raised a new walled town, linking east to Dingyang, and dug a deep trench to cut the road.

literal: Shao then secretly selected strong men and struck from the north.
idiomatic: Shao then secretly selected strong men and struck from the north.

literal: He also sent men to cross the river in secret and notify those inside Yaoxiang to coordinate inside and out.
idiomatic: He also sent men to cross the river in secret and notify those inside Yaoxiang to coordinate inside and out.

literal: More than a thousand crossed; only then did the Zhou realize.
idiomatic: More than a thousand crossed — only then did the Zhou realize.

literal: Battle was joined and the enemy was routed; Yitong Ruogan Xianbao and others were captured.
idiomatic: Battle was joined and the enemy was routed; Yitong Ruogan Xianbao and others were captured.

literal: The generals all wished to attack the new fortress; Shao said, "That fortress has the river on one side and perilous ground on three — it cannot be taken. Even if we took it, it would be only one town.
idiomatic: The generals all wished to attack the new fortress; Shao said, "That fortress has the river on one side and perilous ground on three — it cannot be taken. Even if we took it, it would be only one town.

literal: Better to build another fortress to block their route, break Fucheng, and join forces against Dingyang — that is the longer plan.
idiomatic: Better to build another fortress to block their route, break Fucheng, and join forces against Dingyang — that is the longer plan.

literal: " Officers and soldiers all agreed.
idiomatic: " Officers and soldiers all agreed.

literal: In the sixth month they shifted the siege to Dingyang; the fortress commander, Kaifu Yitong Yang Fan, held firm and would not yield.
idiomatic: In the sixth month they shifted the siege to Dingyang; the fortress commander, Kaifu Yitong Yang Fan, held firm and would not yield.

literal: Shao climbed a height to survey the fortress and then unleashed troops in a fierce assault.
idiomatic: Shao climbed a height to survey the fortress and then unleashed troops in a fierce assault.

literal: In the seventh month the outer city was taken and heads and captives were heaped up.
idiomatic: In the seventh month the outer city was taken and heads and captives were heaped up.

literal: Shao was then ill in camp; the inner citadel had not yet fallen. He told Prince of Lanling Chang Gong, "This fortress is bound by deep ravines and steep peril on three sides — there is no way out save one point in the southeast.
idiomatic: Shao was then ill in camp; the inner citadel had not yet fallen. He told Prince of Lanling Gao Chang Gong, "This fortress is bound by deep ravines and steep peril on three sides — there is no way out save one point in the southeast.

literal: If the enemy breaks out, it will surely be there. Post elite troops to hold that spot alone and capture is assured.
idiomatic: If the enemy breaks out, it will surely be there. Post elite troops to hold that spot alone and capture is assured.

literal: " Chang Gong then set more than a thousand strong men in ambush at the southeastern ravine mouth.
idiomatic: " Chang Gong then set more than a thousand strong men in ambush at the southeastern ravine mouth.

literal: That night it happened exactly as he had foreseen: the enemy came out of the city, the ambush struck, and they broke completely. Fan and the rest were bound and led away; the whole force was taken.
idiomatic: That night it happened exactly as he had foreseen: the enemy came out of the city, the ambush struck, and they broke completely. Fan and the rest were bound and led away; the whole force was taken.

literal: Shao went out to command the armies and came in to counsel at the inner court; his merit stood highest, and with marriage ties besides, his prestige tilted court and realm.
idiomatic: Shao went out to command the armies and came in to counsel at the inner court; his merit stood highest, and with marriage ties besides, his prestige tilted court and realm.

literal: He excelled in stratagem and was skilled at commanding troops; he won the hearts of officers and soldiers, and on the day of battle every man strove to outdo the rest.
idiomatic: He excelled in stratagem and was skilled at commanding troops; he won the hearts of officers and soldiers, and on the day of battle every man strove to outdo the rest.

literal: By nature he was gentle and cautious, with the bearing of a chief minister.
idiomatic: By nature he was gentle and cautious, with the bearing of a chief minister.

literal: He trained his sons and younger brothers; his household was orderly and solemn; he was famed for filial duty toward his stepmother — among the meritorious great houses of Qi, few could match him.
idiomatic: He trained his sons and younger brothers; his household was orderly and solemn; he was famed for filial duty toward his stepmother — among the meritorious great houses of Qi, few could match him.

literal: Yet he was partial to women; though he held weighty office, he would go about in plain dress.
idiomatic: Yet he was partial to women; though he held weighty office, he would go about in plain dress.

literal: There was a Lady Huangfu, wife of Wei Attendant Gentleman Yuan Yu; when Yu's younger brother Jin plotted rebellion, Lady Huangfu was confiscated to the state.
idiomatic: There was a Lady Huangfu, wife of Wei Attendant Gentleman Yuan Yu; when Yu's younger brother Jin plotted rebellion, Lady Huangfu was confiscated to the state.

literal: Shao admired her beauty and memorialized a firm request; Shizong greatly disliked to refuse him and therefore bestowed her upon him.
idiomatic: Shao admired her beauty and memorialized a firm request; Gao Cheng greatly disliked to refuse him and therefore bestowed her upon him.

literal: He was especially stingy with wealth; even kin and old friends he scarcely gave anything.
idiomatic: He was especially stingy with wealth; even kin and old friends he scarcely gave anything.

literal: His son Shen had married a princess and served more than ten days at home as a provincial assistant — when the business was done and he took leave to return, Shao gave him only a cup of wine.
idiomatic: His son Shen had married a princess and served more than ten days at home as a provincial assistant — when the business was done and he took leave to return, Shao gave him only a cup of wine.

literal: His eldest son Yi succeeded him.
idiomatic: His eldest son Yi succeeded him.

literal: Yi, styled Deyou, had fine presence, understood music fairly well, and was also skilled at riding and archery.
idiomatic: Yi, styled Deyou, had fine presence, understood music fairly well, and was also skilled at riding and archery.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he married the Princess of Yingchuan.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he married the Princess of Yingchuan.

literal: He rose in succession to Acting Right Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat, concurrent Palace Master of Writing, and was sent out as Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: He rose in succession to acting right vice director of the branch secretariat, concurrent palace master of writing, and was sent out as governor of Yan Province.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: His son Baoding succeeded him.
idiomatic: His son Baoding succeeded him.

literal: He married the Princess of Zhongshan; at the end of Wuping he held rank equal to the three excellencies.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Zhongshan; at the end of Wuping he held rank equal to the three excellencies.

literal: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he was Kaifu Yitong Sansi and General of Fast Cavalry; at the beginning of Daye he died as Governor of Rao Province.
idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he was kaifu yitong sansi and general of fast cavalry; at the beginning of Daye he died as governor of Rao Province.

literal: Shao's second son Shen, styled Deshen.
idiomatic: Shao's second son Shen, styled Deshen.

literal: Handsome in appearance, broad and careful — he had his father's manner.
idiomatic: Handsome in appearance, broad and careful — he had his father's manner.

literal: In the Tianbao era he received his father's enfeoffment as Duke of Guzang County.
idiomatic: In the Tianbao era he received his father's enfeoffment as duke of Guzang County.

literal: At the beginning of Daning he was made Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadet.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Daning he was made regular attendant of the palace cadet.

literal: In the second year an edict betrothed him to the Princess of Yongchang; before the marriage the princess died.
idiomatic: In the second year an edict betrothed him to the Princess of Yongchang; before the marriage the princess died.

literal: In the third year of Heqing he was again betrothed by edict to the Princess of Dong'an.
idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he was again betrothed by edict to the Princess of Dong'an.

literal: Because his father repeatedly achieved great merit, he rose in succession to Palace Attendant, General, Grand Rectifier of Yuan Province, with revenue from Zhao Commandery.
idiomatic: Because his father repeatedly achieved great merit, he rose in succession to palace attendant, general, grand rectifier of Yuan Province, with revenue from Zhao Commandery.

literal: When Shao fell gravely ill, an edict enfeoffed Shen Prince of Jibei to comfort him.
idiomatic: When Shao fell gravely ill, an edict enfeoffed Shen prince of Jibei to comfort him.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was Left Vice Director of the Xuzhou Branch Secretariat and Governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was left vice director of the Xuzhou branch secretariat and governor of Xuzhou.

literal: After entering Zhou he was made Grand General and Duke of a commandery; he was executed for an offense.
idiomatic: After entering Zhou he was made grand general and duke of a commandery; he was executed for an offense.

literal: Shao's third son Deju, at the end of Wuping, held rank equal to the three excellencies.
idiomatic: Shao's third son Deju, at the end of Wuping, held rank equal to the three excellencies.

literal: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion with Gao Yuanhai and was put to death.
idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiande of Zhou, at Ye he plotted rebellion with Gao Yuanhai and was put to death.

literal: Shao's fourth son Deheng, at the end of Wuping, was Kaifu Yitong Sansi; at the time of Longhua he was Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Shao's fourth son Deheng, at the end of Wuping, was kaifu yitong sansi; at the time of Longhua he was governor of Ji Province.

literal: After entering Zhou he was made Yitong Grand General.
idiomatic: After entering Zhou he was made yitong grand general.

literal: Shao's seventh son Dekan, in the Wuping era, held rank equal to the three excellencies.
idiomatic: Shao's seventh son Dekan, in the Wuping era, held rank equal to the three excellencies.

literal: At the beginning of Daye of Sui he was Governor of Bian Province and died as Administrator of Runan Commandery.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye of Sui he was governor of Bian Province and died as administrator of Runan Commandery.

literal: Rong's second son Xiaoyan, from youth, was quick-witted and had a graceful bearing.
idiomatic: Rong's second son Xiaoyan, from youth, was quick-witted and had a graceful bearing.
